claim: To stop a plotter painting the screen, replace its store instructions with same-length ones (NOP, or CP (HL) to keep 7 T and the access) so state and timing stay identical to the original.
limit: Not safe when the removed paint was a write the game later reads (Starquake): save and restore those bytes.

evidence.text: Removing only the store instructions made the patched run equal the original in every register at each frame boundary, bar A and F inside the plot and blit loops, which follow the bytes read.
evidence.quote: Removing only the store instructions made the patched run equal the original in every register at each frame boundary

evidence.text: Paint site LD (HL),D became CP (HL), not NOP: 7 T and one access of the cell (the NOP was 3 T a cell faster); a build with only the screen sites stays in lockstep with the plain build for 600 rounds.
evidence.quote: Paint site LD (HL),D -> CP (HL), not NOP: 7 T and one access of the cell, as the write (the NOP was 3 T a cell faster).

evidence.text: A store read instead of written takes the same time to the T state: no pace cost.
evidence.quote: store read instead of written takes the same time to the T state

evidence.text: Replacing one store with NOP keeps instruction counts and the lockstep; a watch at the site still checks the store's would-be effect.
evidence.quote: Replacing one store with NOP keeps instruction counts and the lockstep; a watch at the site still checks the store's would-be effect.

evidence.text: Only screen pixel and attribute write instructions were removed (39697, 39827, 37646, 37653, 37707); the plotters keep running, so all game state stays the original's.
evidence.quote: The plotters keep running, so all game state stays the original's.

evidence.text: The paint ran past the attribute area into 0x5B00, read by collision; save and restore the attributes round the painter instead of removing its stores. A full-memory lockstep found it (b1 frame 5398).
evidence.quote: The paint ran past the attribute area into 0x5B00, read by collision:

next_check: A site check that the replacement bytes at a paint site have the length, T states and memory accesses of the original instruction.
